$description: Wave 5 (W5 Selection) component tokens for RadioCards. Same accent-scarcity reasoning as radio.json/checkbox.json/switch.json (D-001/braun-flat rule 3): the selected card's border/indicator fill uses `color.role.neutral.solid`, NOT `color.action.primary` — a plan/tier picker still renders several cards per view, only one selected, but the group itself isn't 'the single most important interactive element' either. `card.bgChecked` reuses `color.surface.inset` (the same recessed-surface step Listbox's selected option uses, D-024-era listbox.json) so the checked card reads as a consistent 'settled in' surface across both Collection- and Standalone-family selection controls. `card.borderChecked`/`indicator.checkedBg` both alias `color.role.neutral.solid`: border-vs-surface.raised measures 8.71:1 (light) / 7.55:1 (dark), comfortably clearing the 3:1 UI-boundary minimum in both themes; `indicator.checkedIcon` reuses `color.text.onRoleSolid` (the same theme-flipping white/near-black pair Checkbox/Switch/Badge already use) against that same solid fill — 9.39:1 (light) / 7.94:1 (dark), clearing 3:1 by a wide margin. `card.borderDefault` reuses `color.border.hairline` (quiet, unselected card edge, braun-flat rule 1 — no decorative shadow) while `card.borderHover`/`indicator.border` reuse `color.border.interactive` (3.96:1 light / 3.54:1 dark against `surface.raised`, the same D-014 pattern Button outline/Input/Radio/Checkbox/Switch all already use for any border that must clear the 3:1 UI-component minimum) — hover widens to this token as the non-color cue (braun-flat rule 4), exactly like Radio's ring border-width step.
